requirement: Each requirement and example definition badge MUST link to its evidence detail page, and each rendered requirement and example MUST be followed by a "See evidence" link to that page. Each detail page MUST link back to the definition's anchored badge and, when an index exists, to the index. Reference badges MUST continue to link to the definition. These links MUST resolve when a requirement name contains `.md`, as in `requirements.cli.mdbook`.
rationale:
The sources satisfy `requirements.index.navigation`. The implementation covers each obligation and the tests exercise the main cases. I did not run the tests. **Implementation, by obligation** - **Definition badges link to the detail page.** `replace_definitions` (src/lib.rs:278) renders the badge as an `` whenever the `DetailPlan` has a detail path for the name. Without a plan it falls back to a ``. The href comes from `chapter_href(current, detail_path, None)`. `DetailPlan::detail_path` (src/index.rs:318) supplies the path. - **"See evidence" link.** The same function appends `

See evidence

` after each rendered requirement or example body, including nested ones through recursion. - **Detail page links back to the anchored badge and the index.** `render_detail_page` (src/index.rs:463) emits `[View definition](#habeas--)`. The anchor comes from `DefinitionKind::anchor` (src/lib.rs:82). When an index exists it also emits `[Requirements index](…) · `. - **Reference badges still link to the definition.** `replace_references` (src/lib.rs:373) still links to `target.path` plus the `kind.anchor` fragment. - **Names containing `.md`.** `chapter_href` (src/lib.rs:464) rewrites `.md` to `%2Emd` in the generated href, so mdBook does not treat it as a chapter suffix. The rewrite includes the anchor fragment. A browser decodes `%2E` back to `.`, so it still matches the element id. - **Index rows and populating the book.** The index table rows link to the detail pages, and `DetailPlan::populate` (src/index.rs:328) builds the pages and inserts them into the book. Both are marked `{impl}` for this requirement. - **Marking.** The marking looks complete. Every function that implements part of the obligations carries an `{impl}` for `requirements.index.navigation`. `preprocess_book` and `detail_path` (free function) carry other requirement markers for page creation and path layout. I found no unmarked behaviour that this requirement doesn't specify. **Tests** - `every_definition_gets_a_nested_detail_page_without_an_index` (src/lib.rs:845) covers these points: - badge `href` and "See evidence" link for both a req and an example, including `cli.mdbook`; - exactly 3 "See evidence" links; - a "View definition" link back to the anchor, with `%2Emd` for the `.md` name; - no index link when there is no index. - `index_shows_evidence_states_and_links_generated_chapters` (src/index.rs:1038) covers these points: - the badge `href` on the definition chapter; - index rows linking to the detail pages; - the detail page linking to both the index and the definition anchor. - `links_preserve_requirement_names_containing_md` (src/lib.rs:951) tests `chapter_href` directly in both directions, with and without an anchor, for `requirements.cli.mdbook`. - Reference badges linking to the definition are tested in `references_in_nested_chapters_link_to_the_requirement_definition`. That test is marked for `requirements.references.book_badges` rather than this requirement, but it does verify the behaviour. No FIXMEs or acknowledged gaps appear in the relevant code.
